goal: Give the 12 mobile-channel enrollment routes (2 portals x 2 channels x 3 actions) one shared runner per action and one Channel actor resolver per portal, so the admin/owner chain cannot re-diverge, and close the owner->admin module dependency completely rather than partially.
non_goals: No unification of the two portals' subscription gates (spec §4.2): admin start keeps its strict subscriptionGrantsFullAccess check, admin cancel/disable keep having none, owner keeps resolveWritableAccountForLocation on all three. The resolver returns the gate outcome; the runner never second-guesses it.
No change to the enrollment state machine (src/lib/channels/mobile-enrollment.ts), disconnectChannel's cascade/audit behaviour, or the advisory-lock key `mobile_enroll:<accountId>`.
No schema change, no migration, no new env var, no new feature flag, no new dependency.
No change to GET /api/dashboard/channels or GET /api/admin/businesses/[id]/channels beyond the import path of the flag/env modules they consume.
No change to the channel UI components (ChannelsPanel.tsx, ChannelsClient.tsx, OwnerTelegramWidget) — the wire contract of all 12 endpoints is unchanged except for the §4.3 status change below.

No CHANNEL_GATES channel->gates registry: isEnabled/assertEnvReady stay explicit config fields on the runner. flagOff is collapsed into the runner because it never varies; the other two genuinely vary by channel.
Not touching PR 3 (§5, Overview spec-alignment) — separate branch, separate PR.
Not fixing the pre-existing non-null assertion on TWILIO_WHATSAPP_NUMBER in the wa.me builder; it stays as-is behind assertWhatsAppEnvReady.
user_visible_behavior: Owner POST /api/dashboard/channels/telegram/cancel and /disable return 404 {"error":"not_found"} instead of 403 {"error":"subscription_not_active"} when the owner's location has no billing account (spec §4.3). Same for the two WhatsApp equivalents. This standardises on the status owner start already returns for the identical condition.

Admin POST .../channels/{telegram,whatsapp}/start error responses (400 businessId required, 403 subscription_not_active, 404 not_found) now carry Cache-Control: no-store, private, which they previously lacked. Admin cancel/disable gain the same on their 400/404. Success responses already had it.

Admin POST /api/admin/channels/whatsapp/start emits a wa.me deep link built by stripping every non-digit from TWILIO_WHATSAPP_NUMBER, matching the owner route. A formatted env value such as '+1 (555) 123-4567' previously produced a broken admin link and now produces a working one.
Nothing else changes on the wire: same statuses, same error codes, same JSON bodies, same QR/deepLink/expiresAt success shape on all 12 endpoints.
invariants: Invariant #1 (Vercel = UI only): no runtime import of openai/@anthropic-ai/sdk/bullmq/postgres/the response generator/the worker queue registry is added to src/app/** or src/components/**. The new src/lib/notifications/channels/*-env.ts modules read process.env and return NextResponse only.

Invariant #8 (auth scope is app-enforced): resolveAdminActor scopes by businessId from the request body behind requireAdminWithAal2; resolveOwnerActor scopes by locationId from the SESSION and never from the body. That asymmetry is the security boundary and must not be collapsed into one code path that reads either source.
Invariant #13 (feature flags are server-authoritative): no NEXT_PUBLIC_* companion is introduced for CHANNELS_TELEGRAM_ENABLED / CHANNELS_WHATSAPP_ENABLED; the flag/env modules stay server-only.

Invariant #15 (domain modules receive their DB client explicitly): the runners and resolvers in src/app/api/_shared/channels/ take `sql: postgres.Sql` as a parameter. Only the 12 route.ts composition roots import the singleton from @/lib/db/server. src/lib/notifications/channels/*-env.ts must not import @/lib/db/server at all.

No backwards dependency from src/lib/** into src/app/**: the moved flag/env modules must NOT re-export flagOff from src/app/api/_shared/channels/flag-off.ts. Routes import flagOff separately (or, per the design, the runner calls it internally).

#773 admission chokepoint: every route keeps at most one query in flight per request chain — no Promise.all over sql is introduced. The resolver's account lookup and the runner's transaction remain strictly sequential.

Approval-token discipline (invariant #5, applied to enrollment tokens): the raw enrollment token is generated OUTSIDE sql.begin, only its SHA-256 hash reaches Postgres, and the raw value appears only in the deep link of the response body — never in a log line, never in the error context passed to reportCaughtError.
The withSameOrigin() CSRF wrapper stays on all 12 exported POST handlers.
Every owner surface stops importing from src/app/api/admin/** — verified mechanically, not by inspection.
edge_cases: resolveAdminActor serves both start (needs the subscription gate) and cancel/disable (must NOT gain one). One query shape — the accounts join — with the gate applied only when the caller asks for it. Admin cancel/disable move from `SELECT account_id FROM businesses` to that join; this adds no gate and no second query, but a bug here silently adds a billing gate to admin cancel, which §4.2 forbids.

resolveWritableAccountForLocation returns three kinds and only `no_account` changes status. `blocked` (402 past_due_read_only / 403 subscription_not_active / 403 account_offboarding_blocked) must still be surfaced verbatim with its own status — do not fold `blocked` into the §4.3 404.

`no_account` and `blocked/subscription_not_active` are different conditions that today share a status on owner cancel/disable. After §4.3 they must be distinguishable: missing account row -> 404 not_found; account exists but is cancelled/pending_payment -> 403 subscription_not_active.
Owner routes return 403 no_business when the session carries no locationId, BEFORE any DB read. That check must stay ahead of the account lookup.

The channel flag gate and the env gate run BEFORE authentication on every route today (flag off -> 404 not_found for an unauthenticated caller). That ordering is deliberate — a disabled channel is indistinguishable from a missing route — and must not be reordered behind auth.

assertTelegramEnvReady / assertWhatsAppEnvReady are bypassed entirely when MOCK_EXTERNAL_APIS=true. Moving these modules must preserve that bypass or every local and CI run of the channel suites changes behaviour.

whatsappEnvReady() has a second consumer that is NOT a route: src/app/(authenticated)/settings/channels/page.tsx and src/app/api/dashboard/channels/route.ts call it for UI availability, so the UI never renders a Connect button the start route would 503. Moving it must keep that consumer working — it is the reason the module belongs in src/lib, not under api/_shared.

The 6 admin route test files mock only @/lib/db/server, @/lib/db/auth, @supabase/ssr, @/lib/auth/mfa and qrcode — they contain ZERO references to the _shared paths. They must therefore pass BYTE-FOR-BYTE unmodified, which is stronger than spec §4.5's 'unmodified except for import paths'. Any edit to them is a signal the refactor changed admin semantics.

The owner test files use a queue-based sql mock where each pushed array is consumed by the next query in order. Changing the NUMBER or ORDER of queries a route issues silently mis-aligns the queue and produces a passing test asserting the wrong thing. resolveOwnerActor must issue exactly the one resolveWritableAccountForLocation query the routes issue today.

src/app/api/dashboard/channels/whatsapp/__tests__/enroll-e2e.integration.test.ts imports ../start/route and drives it through to the worker's twilio inbound handler. It is skipped locally without TEST_DATABASE_POOL_URL and is the only end-to-end proof of the owner start path (spec §7).

The Sentry `endpoint` tag on enrollment DB errors is currently 'telegram/start' (admin) and 'owner telegram/start' (owner). Deriving it from surface+channel+action changes both values. Verified: no alert, dashboard, runbook or code path consumes these tag values.

flagOff() is byte-identical for both channels and both portals (all 12 sites pass the same function). Collapsing it into the runner removes a config field; the response must stay exactly `NextResponse.json({ error: 'not_found' }, { status: 404 })` with no no-store header added, since that is what the existing flag-off tests assert.

disconnectChannel's surface union is 'admin' | 'dashboard' and it composes the cache label as `${surface}.${channel}.disable`. ChannelActor.surface uses those same two values so no mapping layer exists — spec §4.1's 'admin' | 'owner' wording is amended, not implemented.
existing_patterns_to_follow: src/app/api/admin/channels/_shared/start.ts and action.ts — the config-object runner shape (`run*(sql, req, config)`) and the `AdminChannelAccount = { ok: true, ... } | { ok: false, response }` result type that the new resolvers generalise.
src/app/api/admin/channels/_shared/account.ts — the resolve-then-return-inline-Response pattern the ChannelActor resolvers follow.
src/lib/auth/route-helpers.ts requireOwnerWithAccount / requireWritableOwner — the house { ok: true, user, accountId } | { ok: false, response } gate shape and errorResponse()'s always-no-store body.

src/lib/notifications/channels/flags.ts and constants.ts — the destination and naming style for the moved flag/env modules; channelsTelegramEnabled already lives there and isTelegramEnabled is a pure passthrough to it.
src/app/api/zernio/_shared and src/app/api/dashboard/past-replies/_shared — the common-ancestor _shared placement convention for the runner modules.
src/app/api/admin/channels/telegram/__tests__/_shared.test.ts and whatsapp/__tests__/_shared.test.ts — the existing flag/env module test style, which moves with the modules.
src/lib/auth/__tests__/route-helpers.test.ts — the describe(<fnName>) unit-test style for the new resolver tests.

rollback_plan: No schema change, no migration, no flag, no env var — rollback is a straight revert of the squash-merge commit with nothing to un-apply on either Supabase project. The one owner-visible change (§4.3, no_account 403->404 on four endpoints) is reverted by the same commit. Vercel redeploys the previous build; the Railway worker is not in this path.
observability: safeInvalidateChannelCache labels stay distinct per surface in the structured logs: admin.telegram.start / dashboard.telegram.start and the cancel/disable equivalents. A `dashboard.*` label appearing on an admin-initiated action, or the two collapsing to one value, means the ChannelActor surface was mis-wired.

account_audit_log rows written by disconnectChannel keep surface='admin' vs surface='dashboard'. A disable performed from the owner portal that records 'admin' is the same mis-wiring, seen at the audit layer.

Sentry `endpoint` tag on EnrollmentDatabaseError becomes 'admin/channels/telegram/start' / 'dashboard/channels/telegram/start' (previously 'telegram/start' / 'owner telegram/start'). Nothing consumes the old values; the new ones make the portal unambiguous in Sentry.

A 403 subscription_not_active on POST /api/dashboard/channels/{telegram,whatsapp}/{cancel,disable} after this ships means an account row EXISTS and is genuinely not writable — no longer ambiguous with 'no account row at all', which is now 404 not_found. That disambiguation is the §4.3 change observable in prod logs.

The 404 rate on owner cancel/disable should rise by exactly the volume that previously returned 403 with no matching accounts row. A rise beyond that is the §4.3 change catching a wider condition than intended.
allowed_edit_surface_amendments: AMENDMENT 1 (owner-approved 2026-08-15, step 5): added scripts/ci/admin-aal2-audit.ts, its test, and scripts/ci/process-env-baseline.ts. The refactor renamed the helper the admin-aal2 audit tracks and moved the two files the process-env ratchet baselines, so both CI audits fail without these edits. The aal2 change is NOT a rename: the old GATED_SHARED_HELPERS named three admin-ONLY runners that always called requireAdminWithAal2; their successors are portal-agnostic and call config.resolveActor, so naming a runner would let an admin route bind resolveOwnerActor and pass the audit while skipping MFA step-up. The list now names resolveAdminActor, the function that actually calls the gate — strictly stronger than what it replaces. This is the FIRST amendment; a second triggers the abort criteria.
verification_commands_note: The frozen-six guard originally used the DIRECTORY path .../telegram/__tests__, which also contains _shared.test.ts — a file Task 3 deliberately moved — so it reported a break that was by design. It now names the six route suites explicitly. It also no longer exits 1: the six suites carry an owner-approved 6-line fixture amendment (deviations file, Task 6 verdict), so the command reports the diff for review instead of failing the gate on an approved change.
